title: A City of Marble
objective: After this level you can describe how Augustus rebuilt Rome and why buildings mattered politically.
summary: Augustus restored temples, Agrippa built baths and the first Pantheon, and the Ara Pacis celebrated peace. Every building sent a message.

cards.headline: “I found Rome a city of brick and left it a city of marble.”
Building an image
cards.body: According to the historian Suetonius, Augustus boasted that he found Rome a city of brick and left it a city of marble. By his own count in the Res Gestae, he restored 82 temples in a single year. His buildings advertised his piety and linked his rule to Rome’s gods.

cards.headline: A friend who built
cards.body: Augustus’ friend Agrippa paid for major public works in Rome, including baths and aqueducts. He also built the first Pantheon. The domed Pantheon standing today is a later rebuilding under the emperor Hadrian.

cards.fact: The Ara Pacis, the Altar of Augustan Peace, was dedicated in 9 BCE.
cards.context: Its carvings show members of Augustus’ family in procession, a family portrait in marble celebrating the peace he had brought.

cards.headline: Rome: rebuilt
learned: Augustus boasted of a city of marble
He restored 82 temples in one year
The Ara Pacis celebrated his peace

questions.prompt: How many temples did Augustus say he restored in a single year?
questions.explanation: In the Res Gestae, Augustus says he restored 82 temples in one year.

questions.prompt: Why did Augustus pour money into temples and monuments?

options.label: Rome had almost no stone buildings before him
options.rationale: He boasted of turning brick to marble.

options.label: To show his piety and tie his rule to the gods
To house the Senate’s new members
To prepare Rome for a siege

questions.explanation: His buildings advertised his piety and the peace he had brought.

questions.prompt: From Level 7: Roman religion aimed to keep the pax deorum. What was it?

options.label: A temple to the god of war
options.rationale: It was a relationship, not a building.

questions.explanation: The pax deorum was the peace between Rome and its gods, kept by correct ritual. Restoring temples served it.
